key_insight: The paper shows that entanglement entropy and non-stabilizerness (“magic”) can be estimated directly from ZX-diagrams via a flow-based normal form, avoiding expensive full tensor contractions.
engineering_relevance: This gives a scalable way to quantify quantum resources in large circuits, making ZX-calculus more practical for analyzing simulation cost, circuit design, and many-body quantum dynamics.
method: Use flow to rewrite ZX-diagrams into a normal form with a graph-state backbone plus non-Clifford Pauli gadgets.
Derive additive upper and lower bounds on bipartite entanglement entropy from this decomposition.
Preprocess to remove or merge redundant non-Clifford contributions, and use the same form to upper-bound logarithmic stabilizer extent.
evidence_signal: The authors benchmarked the bounds on random unitary and monitored circuits, plus Trotterized Hamiltonian-evolution circuits with Clifford layers, and report that the estimates remain informative at large qubit counts, depths, and spider counts.
watch_item: The result provides bounds rather than exact values, so accuracy depends on how well the ZX normal form captures the circuit structure and on the quality of the preprocessing.
paper_title: Entanglement entropy and magic of ZX-diagrams
